title: Crests and Cairns
summary: Ila's weather has gone stale — a forecast repeated too many times spoils like milk, she says. Stand quiet at the three high places — dune overlook, crater rim, Windspine crest — and bring her back what the horizon says now.

objectives.label: Read the horizon from the dune overlook
Read the horizon from the Choir's crater rim
Read the horizon from the Windspine crest

offer.text: Courier, courier, caught in my chorus — my weather's gone thin, my verses borrowed. Three high places keep the sky's account; go stand where the tall water starts.
The overlook first, where Saltmouth ends. The rim, where the Choir listens down. The crest, where the wind keeps its ledger. Stand still, count slow, remember gold.

accept.text: Still as stone, soft as sand — let the view arrive, don't demand it. I'll pay you in coin now and a verse later. The verse is the better currency, love.

complete.text: Yes — smell of cold iron on the east line, a violet bruise past the ridge... you brought it whole. Three cairns climbed, three skies named, one old singer un-ashamed.
I mostly stood there going quiet. Whatever the desert does next, it talks to you first.
It talks to whoever holds still long enough to be addressed. The first couriers learned that — now you have too.

choices.prompt: Ila asks what you'll remember of the crest.

options.text: "The wind up there keeps accounts. I'll ride like it audits."
"Honestly? The quiet. I didn't know a machine this loud could carry any."
